tasks.short: Work out the load the equipment must meet, look up heat pump and compressor options, compare them, make the selection and check stock and delivery time.

steps.what: Geothermal technician works out the heating and cooling load the equipment must meet
Geothermal technician looks up heat pump and compressor options in supplier datasheets
Geothermal technician compares the options on capacity, efficiency, noise and price
Geothermal technician makes appropriate selections of equipment
Geothermal technician phones the wholesaler about stock and delivery time

tasks.design: A load calculator in the design software ({OTHER}) turns the survey data into heating and cooling loads. The supplier catalogue ({PROCUREMENT}) filters heat pumps and compressors on capacity, refrigerant, noise and size, and shows the shortlist side by side with stock and delivery times from the wholesaler's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}). The selection stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loads were worked out in spreadsheets and options looked up in PDF datasheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Design software calculates loads, and supplier catalogues filter equipment and show stock.
tasks.still_hard: Datasheet figures do not always match real performance in Dutch soil.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a quieter unit because the bedroom is next to the plant room.

reach.learn: Whether stock data cut installation delays.

evidence.claim: Design software calculates heating and cooling loads, and supplier catalogues filter equipment by specification.
Leak checks and logbook rules in the F-gas Regulation bind equipment with fluorinated refrigerants.

assumptions: Boundary: from the site survey to a delivery date; ordering is outside.
Input contract: survey data from the technician's visit; catalogue data from suppliers; stock from the wholesaler's portal; fallback is datasheets and phone.
Suppliers without catalogue data are looked up by hand.

already_counted.description: Geothermal technician checks the load inputs.
Geothermal technician reads the filtered options.

incremental.description: Geothermal technician keeps catalogue filters current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Suppliers without catalogue data save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Survey the property, enter the site data, size the loop and piping, draw the layout, check the design against regulations and explain it to the customer.

steps.what: Geothermal technician surveys the property characteristics on site
Geothermal technician types site notes and measurements into the design file
Geothermal technician sizes the loop and piping for the heating and cooling requirements
Geothermal technician designs and lays out the geothermal heat system
Geothermal technician checks the design against applicable regulations and fills in the notification form
Geothermal technician explains the design to the customer

tasks.design: A mobile survey form ({OPS_SYSTEM}) captures site data and photos straight into the design file. The design software ({OTHER}) sizes the loop and piping from the loads and soil data and starts the layout from standard templates for common house types. A checklist with the notification fields fills from the design for the technician to check. Surveying, final layout choices and explaining stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site notes were retyped, sizing done in spreadsheets and forms filled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile survey forms and design software with loop sizing and templates are available.
tasks.still_hard: Older houses rarely fit a standard template.
tasks.human_edge: Routing pipes around a listed garden wall.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks a sized design instead of calculating it.

reach.learn: Whether shared design files cut site questions.

evidence.claim: Design software sizes ground loops and piping from loads and soil data.
A closed ground loop must be notified to the municipality before installation, and design and drilling need certified firms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer request to the explained design; drilling is outside.
Input contract: loads from the technician's calculation; soil data from public subsurface maps; templates set by the firm's lead engineer; fallback is spreadsheets.
Surveying and explaining do not change.
Customers' time is outside the technician's savings.
research_questions: Do design revisions after drilling fall?

already_counted.description: Geothermal technician checks the filled notification fields.

incremental.description: Geothermal technician keeps layout templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Older houses need more custom design.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up soil, groundwater and protection-zone data, inspect the plot, compare loop types, determine the most suitable loop and explain the choice to the customer.

steps.what: Geothermal technician looks up soil, groundwater and protection-zone data for the address
Geothermal technician inspects the plot for space and drilling access
Geothermal technician compares vertical, horizontal and open loops on cost, space and yield
Geothermal technician determines the type of geothermal loop system most suitable to the property
Geothermal technician explains the loop choice to the customer

tasks.design: Entering the address in the design software ({OTHER}) pulls soil layers, groundwater depth and protection zones from public subsurface maps ({GOV_PORTAL}) into one summary. A comparison sheet computes cost, space needed and expected yield for each loop type from the plot data. Inspecting the plot, choosing the loop and explaining the choice stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Map data were looked up on several public sites and compared by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Public subsurface maps can be read by address, and calculators compare loop types.
tasks.still_hard: Local soil can differ from the maps; drilling may still surprise.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the only drilling spot is under a tree the customer loves.

reach.learn: Whether address look-ups speed up first quotes.

evidence.claim: Public subsurface and groundwater maps can be queried by location.
Open loops that pump groundwater need a permit, and protection zones can rule drilling out.

assumptions: Boundary: from the address to the explained choice; detailed design is outside.
Input contract: map data from public sources; plot data from the technician's visit; fallback is looking up each site.
Inspecting, choosing and explaining do not change.
Map data are checked against what drilling finds.
research_questions: How often does drilling contradict the map summary?

already_counted.description: Geothermal technician reads the map summary.
Geothermal technician checks the comparison sheet.

incremental.description: Geothermal technician reports map gaps to the lead engineer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is on-site judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The geothermal technician keeps surveys, choices and customer talks; look-ups, spreadsheets and retyping shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who quotes a sound design on the day of the visit.
